job: Show and hide sections of text so a long page stays short.
purpose: A list of native details elements. Each item has a trigger row and a panel; Fire animates the height. It works without script and with the keyboard. data-single keeps one item open. The disclosure is the single-item form: one inline toggle that reads as text.
useWhen: A page answers several questions and most readers need only one: FAQs, request headers, response body, timing.
Secondary detail should stay one click away without leaving the page.
One piece of optional detail sits inline in a sentence or a card: use the disclosure form.

avoidWhen.when: The sections are peers that people switch between and compare.
One metric with a hidden breakdown, such as credits remaining.
A table row has detail that belongs to that row.
The content is a short list of actions or choices.

states.name: open
states.how: data-state="open" on the details element, set by script; the native open attribute stays in step

states.name: closing
states.how: data-state="closing" while the height animates shut

states.name: single-open
states.how: data-single on fd-accordion; opening one item closes its siblings

variants.useWhen: The accordion sits on its own as a framed block of FAQs.
The chevron comes before the label instead of after it.

parts.role: The summary row that toggles the item.
Inner wrapper that carries the padding.
Inner wrapper of the disclosure panel.

keyboard.does: Toggles the focused item (native summary behaviour).
